takeaway: Subscapularis is the rotator cuff muscle responsible for internal rotation of the arm, so its injury causes weak internal rotation.

lines.text: A 23-year-old man falls onto his left shoulder while playing rugby.
lines.say: A twenty-three-year-old man falls onto his left shoulder while playing rugby.

lines.text: He has pain throughout the shoulder after the fall.
When internal rotation of the arm is tested, it is weaker than on the other side.
Internal rotation of the arm is the job of subscapularis.
An injury to the subscapularis tendon explains his weakness.
Subscapularis is part of the rotator cuff.
So weak internal rotation of the arm points to the subscapularis tendon.
Remember: subscapularis turns the arm inwards.
